scope: Wan preprocessing diagnosis and fail-closed support recovery for the unscrew-cap and rinse-bottle drivers
summary: The unmodified Wan preprocessing attempts failed before generation because SAM2 returned empty driver masks. A first direct diagnostic utility also segfaulted, while a process-local diagnostic hook isolated the empty ranges. Difference-supported replacement bundles removed every empty frame; the broad v1 bundles were rejected and the narrower v2 bundles were admitted only as generation inputs.
evidence: The immutable failed runs are full/unscrew-bottle-cap/20260811T103608Z-4c6944ce and full/rinse-bottle/20260811T103609Z-eebba045; neither produced a candidate video.
The process-local hook reports 164 empty unscrew frames in ranges 2-59, 61-119, and 121-167, and 118 empty rinse frames in ranges 121-179 and 181-239.
The threshold-48/dilation-9 v1 support covered about 81-82% of frames on average and was rejected as too broad before generation.
The threshold-64/dilation-3 v2 support has zero empty frames, 56.99% mean coverage for unscrew, and 63.59% for rinse.
lessons: A realistic generated robot driver can still violate a segmentation model's subject prior; preprocessing validity must be checked independently of perceived driver quality.
The fallback must be fail-closed but bounded: preserving every action frame is necessary, while excessive whole-frame support risks avoidable background redraw and blur.
limitations: The replacement support is camera-frame appearance-driven rather than a semantic robot instance segmentation result.
This record does not promote either final video; it only admits the v2 bundles to full generation.
next_actions: Complete full Wan generation, then run dense visual and fixed-threshold quality gates before packaging.
